statements.impact_statement: GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx (GO-2026-5774): middleware.RealIP in chi from 5.2.1 took the leftmost X-Forwarded-For address, which a client controls, as the request's RemoteAddr, so a client could spoof its IP address to any handler or rate limiter that relies on it. It affects github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 from 5.2.1 before 5.3.0. Upstream fixed it in v5.3.0 (https://github.com/go-chi/chi/pull/967, https://github.com/go-chi/chi/commit/3b171578ca44dfd75ca3c5cbddc7b44c600a7b49). Sources: https://github.com/go-chi/chi/security/advisories/GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx and https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5774. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 27 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (50 packages). Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). We read the program in full from every package, except 1.26.0-r3, whose program has the same SHA-1 checksum, recorded in its package header, as the 1.26.0-r2 program we read. The -dev program is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath, but it carries the same Go release and module versions as the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same build. Its Go build information, the same on both architectures and with no replacement, gives github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 v5.2.5 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.23.1-r0, v5.3.0 in 1.23.1-r1, v5.3.1 in 1.23.1-r3 to 1.23.1-r6, v5.3.2 in 1.23.1-r8 to 1.26.0-r1, v5.5.0 in 1.26.0-r2 to 1.30.0-r0. The Go function table of every build holds chi router and middleware code (for example the request logger and the response writer wrappers) but not middleware.RealIP, its handler closure RealIP.func1 or the helper realIP; a byte search of every program finds the text RealIP only once, inside the name of the package variable github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.xRealIP (a header-name variable that the package initializer sets), and finds realIP not at all. As a control, the same searches find runtime.main and github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware code in every build, and find middleware.RealIP, RealIP.func1 and realIP in the function table (RealIP 5 and realIP 2 times in a byte search) of a test program we built with the same Go release (go1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) against chi v5.2.5 that installs middleware.RealIP on a chi router. The vulnerable RealIP middleware is therefore not present in this package, including in the builds that carry chi before 5.3.0.

It affects github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 from 5.2.1 before 5.3.0. Upstream fixed it in v5.3.0 (https://github.com/go-chi/chi/pull/967, https://github.com/go-chi/chi/commit/3b171578ca44dfd75ca3c5cbddc7b44c600a7b49). The scout-sbom-indexer-fips-dev packages for Alpine 3.23 are published in the DHI Alpine security repository, which requires authentication, and we have not inspected them for this assessment. Until then this package is under investigation.

It affects github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 from 5.2.1 before 5.3.0. Upstream fixed it in v5.3.0 (https://github.com/go-chi/chi/pull/967, https://github.com/go-chi/chi/commit/3b171578ca44dfd75ca3c5cbddc7b44c600a7b49). Sources: https://github.com/go-chi/chi/security/advisories/GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx and https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5774. The scout-sbom-indexer-fips packages for Debian 13 are published in the DHI Debian security repository, which requires authentication, and we have not inspected them for this assessment. Pending: an inspection of the program in every published build of this package (its Go build information, function table and a byte search, as done for the scout-sbom-indexer packages) to establish which github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 version and whether middleware.RealIP is linked each build carries. Until then this package is under investigation.

statements.impact_statement: GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx (GO-2026-5774): middleware.RealIP in chi from 5.2.1 took the leftmost X-Forwarded-For address, which a client controls, as the request's RemoteAddr, so a client could spoof its IP address to any handler or rate limiter that relies on it. It affects github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 from 5.2.1 before 5.3.0. Upstream fixed it in v5.3.0 (https://github.com/go-chi/chi/pull/967, https://github.com/go-chi/chi/commit/3b171578ca44dfd75ca3c5cbddc7b44c600a7b49). Sources: https://github.com/go-chi/chi/security/advisories/GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx and https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5774. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-oci-config package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 27 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on both architectures (50 packages). The md5sums manifest in each package's control archive lists a single file, /opt/docker/config/scout-sbom-indexer.yaml, whose MD5 checksum is that of the 180-byte YAML configuration file shipped in the Alpine packages (it sets SBOM cataloger options for the image); every package, downloaded in full with its checksum matching the repository index, holds only that file. It contains no program, library or Go code, so github.com/go-chi/chi is not part of this package. The program ships in the scout-sbom-indexer and scout-sbom-indexer-dev packages, which have their own decisions.

GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx (GO-2026-5774): middleware.RealIP in chi from 5.2.1 took the leftmost X-Forwarded-For address, which a client controls, as the request's RemoteAddr, so a client could spoof its IP address to any handler or rate limiter that relies on it. It affects github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 from 5.2.1 before 5.3.0. Upstream fixed it in v5.3.0 (https://github.com/go-chi/chi/pull/967, https://github.com/go-chi/chi/commit/3b171578ca44dfd75ca3c5cbddc7b44c600a7b49). Sources: https://github.com/go-chi/chi/security/advisories/GHSA-3fxj-6jh8-hvhx and https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5774. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 27 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages). Each package installs one file, /sbom-indexer, as listed in the md5sums manifest of its control archive, and the MD5 checksum recorded there equals that of the program we read in full from the Alpine 3.23 package of the same version, revision number and architecture (for example 1.20.4-5 matches 1.20.4-r5; 1.26.0-3 matches the 1.26.0-r2 program, which 1.26.0-r3 also carries), so these packages carry the same statically linked Go programs, built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). Its Go build information, the same on both architectures and with no replacement, gives github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 v5.2.5 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.23.1-0, v5.3.0 in 1.23.1-1, v5.3.1 in 1.23.1-3 to 1.23.1-6, v5.3.2 in 1.23.1-8 to 1.26.0-1, v5.5.0 in 1.26.0-2 to 1.30.0-0. The Go function table of every build holds chi router and middleware code (for example the request logger and the response writer wrappers) but not middleware.RealIP, its handler closure RealIP.func1 or the helper realIP; a byte search of every program finds the text RealIP only once, inside the name of the package variable github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.xRealIP (a header-name variable that the package initializer sets), and finds realIP not at all. As a control, the same searches find runtime.main and github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware code in every build, and find middleware.RealIP, RealIP.func1 and realIP in the function table (RealIP 5 and realIP 2 times in a byte search) of a test program we built with the same Go release (go1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) against chi v5.2.5 that installs middleware.RealIP on a chi router. The vulnerable RealIP middleware is therefore not present in this package, including in the builds that carry chi before 5.3.0.
